Perused the record.
Counter affidavit filed by the learned A.G.A. and the rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for applicant in Court today are taken on record.

Feeling aggrieved by the judgement and order dated 13.1.2023, passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge POCSO Act, Court No.1, Varanasi in Sessions Trial No. 49 of 2015 (State Vs. Ravi Kumar Bhardwaj @ Ravi Rajbhar) arising out of Case Crime No. 88 of 2015, under section 363, 366 and 376 IPC, and 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Cholapur, District- Varanasi,
applicant/appellant has preferred above mentioned criminal appeal.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
By means of above noted judgement and order, applicant/appellant has been convicted under section 363 IPC and consequently, sentenced to three years rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs. 3,000/- and in case of default, applicant/appellant is to undergo one month additional imprisonment, Under section 366 IPC with seven years rigorous imprisonment along with fine of Rs. 5,000/- and in case of default, applicant is to undergo two months additional imprisonment,
Under Section 4 POCSO Act with ten years rigorous imprisonment along with fine or Rs. 20,000/-.
In case of default, applicant is to ungergo one year additional rigorous imprisonment.
Impugned judgement and order further records that a sum of Rs. 20,000/- shall be payable to prosecutrix as compensation,
All the sentences shall run concurrently.
Resultantly, applicant/appellant has filed aforementioned affidavit seeking suspension of sentence/bail during the pendency of appeal.
Learned counsel for applicant contends that applicant/appellant has been convicted under sections 363 and 366 IPC and section 4 POCSO Act.
The Maximum sentence awarded to applicant/appellant is ten years.
Applicant was on bail during pendency of trial.
However, applicant/appellant surrendered before Court below on 12.1.2023.
However, pursuant to judgement and order dated 12.1.2023, applicant/appellant was taken into custody to serve out the sentence.
Applicant/appellant has undergone 4 and 1/2 months of incarceration.

She has then invited the attention of Court to the impugned judgement and on basis thereof she submits that Court below has relied upon School Leaving Certificate of the Prosecutrix, according to which on the date of occurrence, the prosecutrix was aged about 16 years and one month.

However, the said school leaving certificate has not been signed by the Principal of the institution which fact has emerged in the deposition of the Principal of the Institution itself, who has deposed before Court below as P.W.5.
She further submits that as per medical opinion, age of the prosecutrix is 17 and 1/2 to 19 years.
She has then invited the attention of Court to the statement of the prosecutrix under section 161 Cr.P.C. which is noted by Court below at page 21 of the paper book.
Attention of the Court was further invited to the statement of the prosecutrix as recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. which is on record at page 105 of the paper book.
On basis of above, she submits that prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party.
The prosecutrix in her deposition before Court below has reiterated her earlier statements under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
On the above premise, she contends that no offence all alleged can be said to have been committed by applicant/appellant.

sentences.text: In case, the applicant/appelalnt is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.

Per contra, the learned A.G.A., Dr. Abida Syed, the learned counsel for respondents-2 and 3 and Mr.
Laxman Tripathi, the learned counsel for respondent-4, have opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that applicant has been convicted for an offence under section 363, 376 IPC and Section 4 POCSO Act.
As such, applicant is guilty of committing Penetrative Sexual Assault upon the prosecutrix who is a young girl aged about 16 years.
Offence complained of is not private in nature but a crime against society.
Accordingly criminality committed by applicant falls under the category "moral terpitute".
As such interest of justice shall better be served in case the appeal itself is heard on merits by fixing a short date instead of deciding the bail matter.
However, they could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant with referene to record at this stage.

Having heard Ms. Alankita Shukla, along with Mr. I.P. Singh, the learned counsel for applicant/appellant, the learned A.G.A. for State, Dr. Abida Syed, learned counsel for respondents-2 and 3 and Mr. Laxman Tripathi, the learned counsel for respondent-4, upon perusal of material brought on record, evidence as well as, complicity of applicant/appellant and accusation made coupled with the fact that maximum sentence awarded to applicant/appellant is ten years,
applicant/appellant was on bail during pendency of trial, statement of prosecutrix as recorded under section 161 Cr.P.C. as referred to at page 21 of the paper book, her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C (page 105 of paper book) as well as her deposition before Court below, it is apparent that the prosecutrix has remained clear, consistent and categorical in her statements, the prosecutrix has herself accompanied the applicant/appellant, as such, she is a willing and consenting party, the Court below has inferred age of prosecutrix below 18 years of age on the basis of School Leaving Certificate, which has not been signed by Principal of the institution as has been deposed by Principal of the Institution itself, who has deposed before Court below as P.W.5, as per medical evidence, the age of the prosecutrix is 17 years and 6 months to 19 years, the clean antecedents of applicant/appellant as he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one but without making any comment on the merits of the appeal, applicant/appellant has made out a case for bail.
Let the appellant-Ravi Kumar Bhardwaj @ Ravi Rajbhar, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

It is, however, provided that the amount of fine awarded by court below shall be deposited by applicant-appellant with the court below within a period of 1 month from today failing which, the bail granted to applicant-appellant shall stand canceled and he shall be taken into custody at once to serve out the sentence.
Order Date :- 19.5.2023 Arshad  Ravi Kumar Bhardwaj @ Ravi Rajbhar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73353810/
